capabilities.name: Wall / Door / Window / Column / Slab instance recovery from Revit 2024 partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records + partition_schema_mvp::instances_from_partition_category_records / slabs_from_partition_category_records + partition_ifc_export_overrides; tests/project_count_fixtures.rs (IFCWALL 360/360, IFCDOOR 132/132, IFCWINDOW 6/6, IFCCOLUMN 256/256, IFCSLAB 80/80, IFCSHADINGDEVICE 20/20, tolerance 0) and the magnetar-2024-core-interior-slim OctetProof verdict, where entity_counts.IFCWALL / IFCDOOR / IFCWINDOW / IFCCOLUMN / IFCSLAB / IFCSHADINGDEVICE are all inside the claimed surface and rvt-rs, IfcOpenShell and IFClite agree exactly
capabilities.notes: Scope is six BuiltInCategories (OST_Walls, OST_Doors, OST_Windows, OST_Columns, OST_Floors, OST_BuildingPad), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. Selection is a direct byte test, not a heuristic: the record must carry no container reference at +0x32 and placement kind 0xffffef7f at +0x42 (RE-21). It supersedes the #204 column rule, whose family-local bbox proxy and highest-ElementId-per-footprint collapse are removed. RE-22 (#212) extended the same rule to slabs and found it already exact there: its 99 OST_Floors selections are all exported (79 IfcSlab + 20 IfcShadingDevice), and the 80th exported slab is an OST_BuildingPad (Pad:Site Pad, ElementId 21975). The IfcSlab / IfcShadingDevice split is a per-instance Revit 'IFC Export As' override read out of the partition parameter block: the UTF-16LE value string with the owning ElementId as a u64 at -0x0dc and again at -0x11e, both required to agree and to be declared in Global/ElemTable. Thirty-one entries pass on this file, naming 21 ids; the 20 that are also placed instances are exactly the export's IFCSHADINGDEVICE Tag set. Only IfcShadingDevice is honoured as an override target — an unrecognised value leaves the element on its class mapping. Where one ElementId is framed more than once, the record with the greatest bounding-box z extent is kept; that agrees with the export's IfcExtrudedAreaSolid.Depth on 79 of 80 slabs (the 80th is exported as two stacked solids summing to it). Ties go to the newest frame - the greatest (stream, offset) - because Revit rewrites an edited element into a higher-numbered Partitions stream and leaves the earlier copy in place (RE-26): 171 of 360 walls and 96 of 132 doors carry two frames that disagree about the plan box, and on the newest one the wall's thin plan extent equals the nominal thickness of the IfcWallType Revit's export assigns on 360 of 360 (201 of 360 on the oldest) and its type slot equals that IfcWallType.Tag on 356 of 360 (183 of 360 on the oldest; the positional read is superseded by RE-28's set test, which is 360 of 360 - see element-record-wall-type-join). Global/ElemTable's u32 at +0x1c is a monotone version counter that ranks the same way across all 976 exported instances. No frame of any instance on this file disagrees about the box's z, so the tie-break cannot move an element between storeys - storey_bound_elements was 801 either way when this was measured, and is 853 since #219 / RE-27. Column, window, slab and building-pad boxes are unchanged; door boxes move without a measurement that adjudicates them, since a door's record box is not the panel Revit exports and 0 of 132 are world-exact either way. Bodies are the record's own bounding box, not a recovered family profile or wall location curve; for plates the z extent is the real thickness, and since RE-25 (#31) the plan profile of a slab whose sketch closes is the recovered sketch boundary rather than the box rectangle - see element-record-slab-plan-profile. Base/top Level ElementIds stay unbound (#86); doors and windows are attached to their host wall as of RE-23/#222 (see element-record-door-window-host-binding). Storey containment came from the #213 column-derived elevation set when this row landed: walls, doors and columns bound by their record base, plates by their record top face (Revit hangs a floor below its level) — 51 of 100 plates bound and all 51 agreed with the export, none wrongly, while windows never bound because their record base is a sill height, measured 0 of 6. Since #219 / RE-27 the first join tried is the Level ElementId the record itself names, which reaches all 100 plates and all 6 windows; that elevation path survives as the fallback - see record-level-reference-storey-bind. This is not evidence for any other category or release.
capabilities.user_impact: On the recorded Revit 2024 project, walls, doors, windows, architectural columns, floor slabs and building pads come out as placed IFC entities with position, a solid body and (for slabs) a measured thickness and plan profile, matching Revit's own export element for element. On Autodesk's Snowdon Towers 2024 samples most element frames use a second prologue; their ElementIds come from the enclosing partition record (RE-35), and walls, doors, windows, columns and floors export under Revit's own ids (see element-records-second-prologue-ids). Structural framing, structural columns, foundations and generic models export from the same records (see element-records-structural-categories).

capabilities.name: Furniture, casework, fixtures, equipment, ceilings, curtain-wall parts, railings, wall sweeps, ducts and pipes from partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::PRODUCT_RECORD_CATEGORIES; tests/element_records_2025.rs against Drshelden/IFC-ECS RE1 Architecture, Mechanical and Plumbing (MIT, fetched by CI tier 2); examples/probe_re33_category_census.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-33-product-categories.md
capabilities.notes: Thirteen more BuiltInCategory values decode under the unchanged RE-21 instance rule, and every ElementId they select from a record carrying it at +0x00 is a Tag in Revit's own export of the same file: zero false positives on RE1 Architecture, Mechanical and Plumbing (Revit 2025) and on Snowdon Towers (Revit 2024, measured locally). With RE-35's second-prologue ids, RE1 Architecture exports all 58 elements of these categories, RE1 Mechanical all 66 ducts, pipes and fittings and RE1 Plumbing all 117 pipes and fittings and all 6 fixtures, plus one fixture Revit's export leaves out; on Snowdon, curtain panels, railings, ceilings, furniture and fixtures are complete, and 47 curtain panels are elements Revit's export omits (#309). The 60 placed instances with no 3D volume are left out as Revit leaves them out. Second-prologue frames keep the container and placement fields, so the unattributed count covers placed instances only and matches the missing elements exactly for pipes, fittings, mullions, columns, railings, ceilings and furniture. Bodies are the record bounding box; entities are the IFC4 types (IfcFurniture, IfcSanitaryTerminal, IfcCovering, IfcMember, IfcPlate, IfcRailing, IfcBuildingElementProxy, IfcDuctSegment, IfcDuctFitting, IfcPipeSegment, IfcPipeFitting). Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Revit 2024 and 2025 projects export furniture, casework, plumbing fixtures, specialty equipment, ceilings, curtain-wall mullions and panels, railings, wall sweeps, ducts and pipes whose records carry their ElementId, each one an element Revit's own export also holds; the diagnostics count the rest.

capabilities.name: ElementIds for second-prologue partition element records, read from the enclosing partition record
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::partition_record_chain / assign_second_prologue_ids / RevitFile::second_prologue_ids; tests/partition_record_chain.rs (every first-prologue frame starts a record of its own id on Core Interior and the RE1 models); tests/element_records_2025.rs; examples/probe_re35_record_wrapper.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-35-partition-record-wrapper.md; reports/element-framing/RE-43-invalid-element-id.md
capabilities.notes: Every Partitions/* stream opens with a chain of records, one per element: u64 ElementId, u32 size, u16 prologue constant (release constant + 28), u16 count, the body, and a 16-byte trailer that repeats the size (RE-35). A first-prologue frame starts its record; a second-prologue frame (RE-30) sits inside its element's record, so its ElementId is the record's, read rather than inferred. All 30,432 first-prologue frames across nine 2024 and 2025 files start a record of their own id, and the chains hold every declared id on Core Interior and the RE1 models. Records after the chain belong to loaded families' own documents and never export. Against Revit's own exports: RE1 Architecture, Mechanical and Plumbing reach 100% of every recovered entity; Snowdon Towers Architectural exports 6,045 elements, 5,945 in Revit's export (a frame holding u32::MAX, the invalid ElementId, also takes its record's id, RE-43), with every wall, column, door, window, curtain wall and panel, railing, ceiling, furniture item, fixture and generic model of Revit's export attributed once RE-41 declares the ElemTable's second id. The rest are real elements Revit's export leaves out (#309); the 18 in non-primary design options are left out as Revit leaves them out (RE-40). Floors, building pads and ceilings get their ids too. It replaces RE-34's reference-order inference, which gave a door its type's id on a Revit 2025 file outside its hold-outs. Placed instances with no 3D volume are left out, as Revit leaves them out. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Files whose element records mostly lack an ElementId at their start (Autodesk's Snowdon Towers samples, the RE1 models, projects saved incrementally) export their walls, doors, windows, floors, ceilings, columns, curtain-wall parts, railings, furniture, fixtures, ducts and pipes under the ElementIds Revit itself uses; the diagnostics count what is still left out.

capabilities.name: ElemTable records whose two ids differ declare the second
capabilities.evidence: elem_table::declared_ids; examples/probe_re41_elem_table_secondary_ids.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-41-elem-table-secondary-ids.md
capabilities.notes: A 40-byte Global/ElemTable record carries two u32 ids, at +16 and +36. They agree on every record of Core Interior, the RE1 models, teste_export_2025, Projeto1 and the 2016-2023 projects measured. On Autodesk's Snowdon Towers samples (local only) they differ on 84 records (Architectural) and 27 (Structural); there the second is the id of the element's partition record (RE-35) and the Tag Revit's own IFC export writes, and the first is neither. The declared id set now holds both (a 0 in the second is not added), which attributes all 37 element records Snowdon Architectural left unattributed (16 walls, 4 columns, 17 generic models, all in Revit's export) and one floor on Snowdon Structural (in the VIM export). Licensed files export byte-identically. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Elements whose ElemTable record carries a second id, such as those in a primary design option on Autodesk's sample, export under the ElementId Revit itself uses instead of being counted as unattributed.

capabilities.name: Structural framing, structural columns, structural foundations and generic models from partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::PRODUCT_RECORD_CATEGORIES (OST_StructuralFraming, OST_StructuralColumns, OST_StructuralFoundation, OST_GenericModel); examples/probe_re36_vim_oracle.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-36-structural-categories.md
capabilities.notes: Four more BuiltInCategory values decode under the RE-21 instance rule with RE-35's enclosing-record ElementIds and export as IfcBeam (.BEAM.), IfcColumn (.COLUMN.), IfcFooting and IfcBuildingElementProxy. Measured locally on Autodesk's Snowdon Towers 2024 samples, which have no licence and are not in CI. Against the VIM export of the Structural sample (a later edition), every exported id the VIM carries has the record's category there: 914 framing members, 74 columns, 90 foundations and 91 generic models, none under another category. The 28 framing ids it lacks are beam-system members the later edition regenerated. On the architectural sample 260 of 261 generic models are in Revit's own IFC4 export; the other is in a non-primary design option. Framing on that file has no braces (Structural Usage: joists, girders, purlins), so IfcBeam is the entity; a brace would also export as IfcBeam, since the record's structural type is not decoded, and Revit's own PredefinedType is not measured. Rebar, structural connections and beam systems have correct ids but are not exported. Bodies are the record bounding box. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Revit 2024 and 2025 structural models export their beams, joists, girders, columns, footings and generic models as IFC elements under Revit's own ElementIds, with bounding-box bodies; rebar and connections are not exported.

capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::PRODUCT_RECORD_CATEGORIES; tests/element_records_2025.rs against Drshelden/IFC-ECS RE1 Mechanical and Electrical (MIT, fetched by CI tier 2); reports/element-framing/RE-37-fixture-site-circulation-categories.md

Entities follow Revit's IFC4 export on Snowdon (IfcLightFixture, IfcElectricAppliance, IfcBuildingElementProxy, IfcTransportElement, IfcRamp); air terminals use IfcAirTerminal, the IFC4 subtype of the IfcFlowTerminal Revit writes in IFC2x3. Bodies are the record bounding box. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Revit 2024 and 2025 projects export their lighting fixtures, air terminals, kitchen equipment, planting, parking, entourage, hardscape, elevators and ramps as the IFC entities Revit itself uses, each one an element Revit's own export also holds.

capabilities.name: Electrical and mechanical devices and equipment from partition element records, without their nested symbols (RE-79)
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::PRODUCT_RECORD_CATEGORIES and NESTED_COMPONENT_CATEGORIES; partition_schema_mvp::without_nested_components; examples/probe_re79_nested_mep_components.rs; tests/element_records_2025.rs (revit_2025_electrical_devices_are_revits_own); reports/element-framing/RE-79-mep-devices-nested-components.md
capabilities.notes: Six BuiltInCategory values (OST_LightingDevices, OST_FireAlarmDevices, OST_DataDevices, OST_ElectricalFixtures, OST_ElectricalEquipment, OST_MechanicalEquipment) decode under the RE-21 instance rule. A shared nested device (the symbol a switch or receptacle nests) is a record of its own in its parent's category; the two list each other among their references and the nested one has the larger ElementId, and Revit's export leaves it out, so rvt-rs does too (21 of 21 on RE1 Electrical). RE1 Electrical then exports exactly Revit's elements: 12 lighting fixtures, 2 data devices, 5 fire alarm devices and 30 devices and panels, none outside its export; RE1 Mechanical adds its AHU. Entities are the IFC4 subtype of what Revit's IFC2x3 export writes: IfcAlarm (IfcAlarmType), IfcElectricAppliance (IfcElectricApplianceType), proxies. Measured on the RE1 models only; Core Interior and Snowdon Towers hold none of these categories and are unchanged. Bodies are the record bounding box. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: MEP models export their switches, receptacles, sensors, alarms, panels and equipment, each an element Revit's own export also holds.

capabilities.name: Revit 2023 elements from their partition element records: identity, category and box (RE-81)
capabilities.evidence: src/partition_element_records_2023.rs; partition_schema_mvp::recover_2023_records and nested_in_openings; examples/probe_re81_2023_element_records.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-81-2023-element-records.md; RE-107: partition_level_records::find_level_records_2023 / schema_elevation_marker / OWNER_SENTINEL_RUN_LEN_2023, partition_schema_mvp::select_newest_instance_records, tools/re/storeys_vs_ifc.py, reports/element-framing/RE-107-levels-2023.md; RE-111: partition_names::find_element_data_names_2023, partition_schema_mvp::system_type_names_2023, examples/probe_re111_system_types_2023.rs, reports/element-framing/RE-111-system-types-2023.md; RE-112: partition_compound_structure::layer_layout, examples/probe_re112_layers_2023.rs, reports/element-framing/RE-112-layers-2023.md; RE-114: partition_names::ElementDataLayout / element_data_layout, examples/probe_re114_wall_lines_2023.rs, reports/element-framing/RE-114-wall-layers-2023.md; RE-115: partition_materials::CATEGORY_MATERIAL_FRAME_2023 / scan_category_material, examples/probe_re115_category_materials_2023.rs, reports/element-framing/RE-115-category-materials-2023.md; RE-116: partition_materials::frame_at_2023 / scan_material_appearances, partition_schema_mvp::materials_from_records, tools/re/material_colours_vs_ifc.py, reports/element-framing/RE-116-material-colours-2023.md; RE-117: partition_room_parameters::scan_room_parameter_entries, examples/probe_re117_room_names.rs, reports/element-framing/RE-117-room-names.md; RE-119: partition_schema_mvp::resolve_framing_top_levels, tools/re/storeys_vs_ifc.py, reports/element-framing/RE-119-framing-storeys-2023.md; RE-120: partition_schema_mvp::recover_2023_records, element_record_wall_joins::join_trims, reports/element-framing/RE-120-wall-joins-2023.md; RE-122: element_record_beam_cuts::beam_column_trims, examples/probe_re122_beam_column_refs.rs, examples/probe_re122_beam_supports.rs, reports/element-framing/RE-122-beam-column-cuts.md
capabilities.notes: A 2023 record sits behind the schema-derived marker (RE-80) with a u32 ElementId 52 bytes and its BuiltInCategory 38 bytes before it, the rest where 2024 has it, and u32 reference lists. Exported with rvt-ifc against Revit's own IFC4 exports of two local 2023 projects: modelo_bim 37 of 37 elements, none outside the export; Exemplo_data 37 of 45, none outside it, the 8 missing being window trims nested in windows, left out with the mullion patterns Revit also leaves out because nothing decoded tells them apart. Every body is the record's bounding box. Doors and windows bind to their host wall by RE-85's rule on the u32 reference lists: all 19 on Exemplo_data and 11 on modelo_bim take the wall Revit's filled opening voids, and 15 of the 30 openings equal Revit's within 0.01 ft. Not read on 2023: names, types, storeys, joins and profiles, design options, parameters, IFC export overrides (4 spread footings Revit writes as IfcSlab come out as IfcFooting). Einhoven (2023, no Revit export) gains 2 walls, 9 curtain panels and 2 windows, unverified.
capabilities.user_impact: Revit 2023 projects export their walls, doors, windows, floors, roofs, columns, beams, foundations and rooms as typed IFC elements in the right place and size, under Revit's own ElementIds, instead of an empty scaffold. Since RE-107 they also carry Revit's own Levels as storeys, each element on the storey of the Level its record names (since RE-119 a beam on the Level at its top): Exemplo_data 37 of 37 and modelo_bim 37 of 37 in Revit's storey, all 6 storeys Revit's name and elevation. Since RE-109 each family instance carries its family and type name: all 50 doors, windows, columns, beams and footings of the two projects as Revit names them. Since RE-111 each wall, floor and roof carries its type's name (24 of 24 as Revit's), and since RE-112 its type's layers name its system family, so every element Revit's export types is typed with Revit's type Tag: 37 of 37 on each project. Since RE-113 family instances carry their type's materials (Revit's set on 44 of 45), and since RE-114 walls and floors whose layer materials are named carry a material layer set (modelo_bim's 4 walls and floor); since RE-120 walls are cut back by the walls they join, by 2024's join solver (RE-26, RE-29) over the 2023 records, whose reference lists name the joined walls: Exemplo_data's 17 and modelo_bim's 4 walls exact against Revit's export (2 of 17 and 4 of 4 before). Since RE-115 a layer that takes its category's material takes the one 2023's object styles give it (i32 category · ff ff ff ff · u32 1|2 · u32 1 · ff ff ff ff 3f 01 · 8 bytes · i32 -3000010 · u32 material): Exemplo_data's 17 walls and floor, so its elements with Revit's material set are 35 of 37, and modelo_bim's 31 of 37. Since RE-116 2023 materials carry their shading colour, transparency and shininess (a 2024 frame whose four pattern slots are eight bytes, u32 id and u32 COLORREF) and are named as RE-58 names a 2024 material: by its own name field, else the string ending before ff ff ff ff eb 0b (ff ff ff ff 17 0c on 2024); the material list is the file's own materials (Exemplo_data 114, modelo_bim 108, Einhoven 36), Revit's colour and transparency on 20 of the 21 materials the two exports style, none different, and Exemplo_data's elements with Revit's material set are 36 of 37. Since RE-117 2023 rooms carry their number and name, the parameter entries i32 -1006901 (ROOM_NUMBER) and i32 -1006900 (ROOM_NAME) that follow the room's object: 9 of 9 on Exemplo_data as Revit's (see element-record-room-recovery). Since RE-122 a beam stops at the face of each column its record names and holds its end, as Revit's export stops it: modelo_bim's 8 beams exact (their boxes ran to the column centres before).

capabilities.name: Stairs as IFC aggregates of their runs, landings and stringers, and roofs
capabilities.evidence: partition_schema_mvp::attach_aggregate_wholes; IfcEntity::Aggregate and the STEP writer's IfcRelAggregates; examples/probe_re39_stair_parts.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-39-stair-aggregates.md
capabilities.notes: A stair's runs, landings and stringers name the stair's ElementId in their reference lists. Each stair exports as a bodiless IfcStair and its parts (IfcStairFlight, IfcSlab .LANDING., IfcMember .STRINGER.) are related to it by IfcRelAggregates, not contained in a storey. Measured locally on Snowdon Towers Architectural, which has no licence and is not in CI: the same 26 stairs aggregate as in Revit's IFC4 export, and every one of the 228 parts rvt-rs attaches is in the matching Revit aggregate; all 256 new elements (27 stairs, 42 flights, 17 landings, 170 stringers) are in Revit's export. Railings stay standalone: Revit aggregates 65 of the 70 that name a stair, and nothing read tells the other five apart. PredefinedTypes are left unset. Roofs (OST_Roofs) export as one IfcRoof each with the record box: all 20 Snowdon roofs are IfcRoof Tags in Revit's export, which decomposes 7 of them into a same-Tag IfcSlab .ROOF. part that rvt-rs does not reproduce. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Stairs come out as Revit exports them: one IfcStair per stair holding its flights, landings and stringers, so IFC viewers show and select a stair as one assembly.

System families (walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, stairs, railings, curtain walls) have no name entry and keep Class-ElementId names and no ObjectType; their type names come from the type's own element data (RE-44, element-record-system-type-names). capabilities.notes: A system-family type has no RE-38 name entry. Its serialised element data opens with ff ff ff ff, a u16 header word (0x02d3 on Revit 2024, 0x02ef on Revit 2025), 01 00 00 00 and the type's u64 ElementId, and its name is the first framed string after that (ff ff ff ff, a u16 tag other than 0xffff, a u32 length, UTF-16). An element's type is the one type-definition record of its own category its reference list names (RE-28); on Snowdon and RE1 most such records are second-prologue frames that take their partition record's id (RE-35), and on 2025 they carry the 2025 marker and prologue constant. The element's property set gains TypeName. Every name written equals the type half of Revit's ObjectType for the same Tag: 460 on Core Interior (360 walls, 99 floors, the pad), 1,545 on Snowdon Towers Architectural, 16 on RE1 Architecture, 1 on Projeto1, and 6 of 7 on teste_export_2025, where the seventh wall's frame, data and bounding box all describe the other type, so that export was made from a later state of the model. The system family's own name (Basic Wall, Floor) is not stored in the file - the Portuguese export writes Parede basica for the same family - so no FamilyName is written, the IFC Name stays Class-ElementId and ObjectType stays unset. Types with no element-data block stay unnamed: RE1's one railing type and 7 of 22 Snowdon railing types. No other field of the type's data is read; since RE-110 each typed element is typed by an IFC type object of its type (see ifc-type-objects). Revit 2024 and 2025; since RE-111 (2026-09-28) also Revit 2023, whose data header is ff ff ff ff c0 02 01 00 00 00 with a u32 ElementId and whose types have no type record: an element's type is, of the named ids its record names with no record or name entry, the one named by records of a strict subset of the categories naming each of the others; Exemplo_data 18 of 18 and modelo_bim 6 of 6 walls, floors and roofs with Revit's type name. RE-63 (2026-09-24): the system family itself is derived, since Revit stores none - a curtain wall is a Curtain Wall, a railing a Railing, a floor a Floor, a building pad a Pad, and a wall, ceiling or roof whose type has compound layers (an element of the type drawn in layers, or the type's own data) a Basic Wall, Compound Ceiling or Basic Roof - so these elements are named Family:Type:ElementId with ObjectType Family:Type as Revit names them: Snowdon 1,077 of 1,077 walls, 42 of 42 curtain walls, 68 of 68 ceilings, 20 of 20 roofs, 101 of 131 railings (the others have no type name), 167 of 182 floors (the 15 are floors Revit exports in two parts); Core Interior 460 of 460; RE1 16 of 17. RE-64 (2026-09-24): a curtain panel whose cell holds a basic wall keeps the panel category, and its record names one wall type rather than a panel type; the panel takes it when that type has compound layers, and its family is Basic Wall - Snowdon 18 of 18 named as Revit names them, while 23 panels naming a wall type without layers, which Revit's export leaves out, stay unnamed. Slab edges and ramps take their only system family (Slab Edge, Ramp): Snowdon 59 of 59 slab edges named as Revit names them, and both ramps with Revit's ObjectType (Revit adds a :1 part suffix to the ramp's Name). RE-65 (2026-09-24, Revit 2024): stair, landing and support types are serialised like run types (tag db 0f) and keep their name and a family flag at their own offsets - stair type construction u32 +0x129 (0 Assembled Stair, 1 Cast-In-Place Stair; 2, Precast, unmeasured and unnamed), its parameter entries then name from +0x13f and its component types in seven u64 slots from +0xc9; landing flag +0x95 (0 Non-Monolithic Landing) and name +0x98; support flag +0x89 (0 Stringer, 1 Carriage) and name +0x92; a run's family is Monolithic or Non-Monolithic Run by RE-52's flag. A stair is named Family:Stair:ElementId and each part '<stair> Run|Landing|Stringer N', N its ElementId rank among every record of its category naming the stair. Where a part names two types or two stairs, the pair its stair's type lists decides. Snowdon: 26 of 26 stairs, 43 of 43 runs, 17 of 17 landings, 170 of 170 supports with Revit's Name (any of the copies Revit writes of a multistory stair) and ObjectType; Snowdon only, since no other oracle has stairs. RE-66 (2026-09-24, Revit 2024): a railing type with no element data keeps its name in its type object (tag db 0f), as the u32-length UTF-16 string ending at the first ff ff ff ff 0b 02 past +0x100 (+0x1ae on 18 of Snowdon's 20 railing types, +0x1cb on the 2 that carry a Uniformat code); read only where the element-data name is missing. Snowdon railings named as Revit names them: 131 of 131 (was 101); on the 14 types with both, the two names agree. RE-67 (2026-09-24, Revit 2024): model text is a Generic Model that is not a family instance; its list names one text type, a type object (tag db 0f) that frames its name with tag 0x0149 and then a font with tag 0x07eb. It is named Model Text:<type>:<ElementId>: Snowdon 7 of 7 as Revit names them; no other local file has model text. RE-69 (2026-09-24, Revit 2024): a wall sweep's type has no type-definition record of OST_Cornices; it is the one id the sweep's record names that has a type object (tag db 0f) and no name entry, named by its element data, and the sweep is Wall Sweep:<type>:<ElementId>; a sweep naming none is a sweep of a wall type's structure and is named by its ElementId alone, as Revit names it. Snowdon: 258 of 258 wall sweeps named as Revit names them (249 typed, 9 by ElementId). A system family's own name is not in the file; Revit writes it in the locale the file was saved in (BasicFileInfo's Locale when saved). On the four PTB files (two Revit 2023, two Revit 2025) Revit's export names walls Parede básica, floors Piso and roofs Telhado básico, and rvt-rs does too (32 of 32, RE-123); other families and locales keep the ENU name, which is unmeasured outside ENU.
capabilities.user_impact: Walls, floors, ceilings, roofs and railings show the type name Revit gives them (for example 8" Interior Partition 3 Hour or Basement Slab) in the IFC property set and the viewer.

capabilities.notes: Revit's four IFC export parameters are entries i64 BuiltInParameter, u32 n, UTF-16 value in an element's serialised data: IFC_EXPORT_ELEMENT_AS (-1019014), IFC_EXPORT_ELEMENT_TYPE_AS (-1019015), IFC_EXPORT_PREDEFINEDTYPE (-1019016) and IFC_EXPORT_PREDEFINEDTYPE_TYPE (-1019017), public BuiltInParameter values. An entry belongs to the declared element whose element-data header (RE-44) is the last one before it, at most 0x800 bytes back (0x1ac measured); a value must have the shape of an IFC entity name or an enumerator. An element exports as its own override, else its type's (IfcCoveringType naming IfcCovering), with its own predefined type, else its type's, written only when it is an IFC4 enumerator of that entity. Honoured entities are the ones a reference export demonstrates: IfcShadingDevice (RE-22), IfcSlab and IfcCovering. IfcSpace and IfcFooting overrides exist on Core only on elements Revit does not export and stay unhonoured. Revit's own category-to-entity mapping table is not read, and no IfcSlabType or IfcCoveringType is written. Revit 2024 and 2025.

capabilities.notes: A structural-framing element's data carries its location line as a bounded line record: 04 00 08 01, start and end parameters (f64 ft), an origin (3 f64, model ft) and a unit direction (3 f64), found in the data up to the next element-data header. With the element's record box, beam_body solves a box length x width x depth along the line: the length is the line's, the depth comes from the vertical extent, the width from one plan extent, and the other plan extent must come out to 0.01 ft. A level beam exports as Extrusion::rectangle(length, width, depth) rotated to the line's plan angle; a sloped one keeps its record box as the extrusion and sweeps its section along its centreline (SolidShape::SweptPath, IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid with +Z as the fixed reference). On Snowdon Towers Structural (local only) all 942 exported framing elements carry a line, 940 inside their box, and 923 solve (802 level on a model axis, 111 level rotated in plan, 10 sloped); IfcOpenShell meshes each exported solid to its record box (938 to 0.001 ft, 4 to 0.0016 ft). Against the meshes of the 2027 edition's VIM export, scored only where that edition kept the beam's Location, type and mesh consistent (839), the section across the line equals Revit's on 613 and Revit's less the top a floor join cuts on 179; the ends equal Revit's on 485 and Revit trims 352 at their supports (median 0.625 ft at the larger end), which is not read. Rotated beams' solids are 1.108 times Revit's own beam envelope at the median, against 8.406 times for the record box they replace. Status is partial: ends are not trimmed, floor-join cuts are not applied, the section is a rectangle envelope, 17 beams (15 oblique with skewed ends) keep their box, and no licensed CI file has structural framing. Revit 2024 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Beams, joists and girders export along their own axes instead of as boxes around them, so a diagonal beam is a beam, not a slab of the bay it crosses. Since RE-103 a steel beam whose type stores an I section is that I (IfcIShapeProfileDef), flanges across and web upright: 377 of Snowdon Towers' 942 framing elements, and on all 271 its VIM export can score, Revit's own mesh has the section's corners, flange tips and web faces where rvt-rs puts them. Channels, angles, joists and concrete beams keep their box along the line. Since RE-104 a structural column whose type stores an I section is that I turned to the column's own X axis: all 40 of Snowdon Towers' steel columns, and Revit's own mesh on all 24 its VIM export can score. Since RE-105 each of those 417 members is written with an IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage whose IfcMaterialProfile pairs its type's material with its I.

capabilities.notes: A roof's OST_SketchLines records carry the roof's ElementId as their owner reference, as a floor's do (RE-25), and close into its plan outline under the same box solve. A sketch line's element data also carries the bounded line record RE-49 reads for beams (04 00 08 01, start and end parameters, origin, unit direction), so its exact ends are known. Where the box solve does not close an element, its lines' recorded ends are chained into loops, provided every line is level with both ends in its own record's box and every end is shared by exactly two lines; otherwise the element keeps no profile. Profiles that closed before are unchanged. Measured on Snowdon Towers Architectural (local only) per Tag against the upward-face plan area of Revit's own IFC4 geometry (IfcOpenShell 0.8.5): 13 of 20 roofs carry an outline (none did), 6 equal to Revit's area, 5 equal per layer (Revit writes layered roofs as stacked layer solids) and 2 larger (5.4% and 34.7%, cut in Revit's geometry); every roof outline's plan box is its record box. Slabs rise from 117 to 132 of 199 with an outline (149 since RE-96, below); the 15 added are 11 equal (4 outright, 7 per layer) and 4 larger by 0.2% to 3.0%, the shaft-opening residual earlier outlines also show. RE-56: each roof sketch line's data carries its edge's slope angle (9:12 by default) and flags (00 00 01 00, or 01 01 01 00 on an edge that defines the slope, followed by -rise/run); a roof type's layers follow its name and u32 0. A 2024 roof with exactly one defining edge is drawn rising from it at its slope with its type's thickness square to the slope, as an IfcFacetedBrep, only when that reproduces its record box height within 1e-4 ft: on the Autodesk tutorial house (local only) the one sloped roof, 1:12 over 20.458 ft with a 1.25 ft type, gives 2.9591938797 ft against the recorded 2.959193880 ft. Status is partial: hip and gable roofs (two or more defining edges) and roofs sloped some other way (Snowdon's 2112673 has no defining edge but is sloped in Revit's export) stay level plates of their record box's height, cuts are not subtracted, 7 roofs keep their box, no licensed CI file has a roof, and the recorded ends are read on Revit 2024 only. RE-96: a sketch line's curve can be an arc in RE-75's layout without the u64 1 that marks a wall's arc; it counts where every point of it, drawn as chords within 0.0005 ft, lies in the line's record box and the record does not also hold as a line, and an outline with an arc is kept only where it spans its element's record box within 0.001 ft. On Snowdon Towers 17 more slabs carry an outline (132 to 149 of 199): 14 within 0.1% of Revit's upward-face area, 2 half of it (Revit writes each as two solids) and 1 0.8% larger (a tessellated face set in Revit's export); slabs within 0.1% go from 73 to 87. RE-97: a Sketch element's data names the sketched element at +77 and lists its curves (u32 n, n x (u64 id, u32 key), keys rising, with gaps where curves were deleted); where a sketch's list differs from the lines whose owner reference names the element (55 of 447 on Snowdon Towers), the list is the membership, and the outline is kept only where it spans the element's record box. On Snowdon 176 of 199 slabs and all 20 roofs carry an outline (149 and 13 before); slabs within 0.1% of Revit's upward-face area go from 89 to 102 and roofs from 7 to 10 (plan_profiles_vs_ifc.py now takes every piece with one Tag together, which re-scores main from 87 to 89). RE-98: ceilings take their sketch's outline through the same path. Measured on each element's top surface (Revit writes a layered ceiling as one stacked solid per layer, each with the outline): 66 of Snowdon Towers' 68 ceilings within 0.1% of Revit's area (50 before, the rectangles their box already drew), and all 6 of RE1 Architecture's (Revit 2025, 5 before). RE-99: shaft openings (OST_ShaftOpening, -2000996) are sketched as floors are, their sketches holding the two crossing diagonals Revit draws in plan besides the boundary; without those, 8 of Snowdon's 9 shafts close, and each is cut as a void from the one-piece floors, roofs and ceilings within its height that hold it strictly inside: 7 elements on Snowdon, all closer to Revit's area (2 slabs now exact). A shaft on an element's edge, which Revit cuts as a notch, is not cut. Measured on each element's top surface, 150 of Snowdon's slabs are within 0.1% of Revit's area. RE-100: a sketch line that is a full circle is stored in the arc layout under tag 04 00 08 00 with both angles 0; shaft 903725 is one, and read it cuts its round void from 5 more elements, taking Snowdon's slabs within 0.1% of Revit's area to 154.
